cases.prompt: Drive a two-PR Graphite stack bottom-up: PR 101 is the lower dependency and has one pre-existing unresolved thread; PR 102 is its descendant and has none. For each current head, read canonical head and threads, address pre-existing threads before invoking exactly one /woostack-review <PR#> pass, then address all new findings. PR 101 review is clean; PR 102 review has two nits that Address resolves with evidence replies and no code or head change. Return one JSON object with order, addressCalls, reviewCalls, rounds, threads, and status.
cases.expected: PR 101 is addressed before one review and PR 102 is reviewed once; nits resolved on the unchanged PR 102 head do not trigger re-review; both PRs are clean in bottom-up order.

cases.prompt: Drive a three-PR Graphite stack bottom-up. PR 201's one review finds blocker B1; Address resolves it with new code, and descendants PR 202 and PR 203 require restacking. After reading back every affected head/base/ancestry, repeat one Review then Address for PR 201 on its new head; the second review is clean. Return complete evidence for heads, restack, review calls, thread replies/resolutions, and status.
cases.expected: A code-producing blocker round restacks affected descendants and reviews the new PR 201 head before another Address stage; all current heads and thread evidence are read back before the stack is clean.

cases.prompt: Classify a sweep where exact PR 301 has the same blocker fingerprint B7 on the same head sha-301 in two successive rounds. There is no new code, verification, or reviewer evidence. Do not run another review or claim progress. Return one JSON object with status, reviewCalls, blocker, and safeResumeBoundary.
cases.expected: The sweep halts on the unchanged recurring blocker without another round and reports the exact blocker and resume boundary.

assertions.expected: new code or evidence on PR 301

cases.prompt: Resolve three /woostack-sweep targets from the current Graphite graph without changing source control: `adam/exact` is one exact submitted branch bound to canonical PR 401, `feature` is not exact and could refer to two branches, and `adam/local-only` is one exact but unsubmitted branch. Never infer a target or submit a missing PR. Return one JSON object with targets.exact, targets.ambiguous, and targets.unsubmitted.
cases.expected: Only the exact submitted branch binds PR 401; the inferred ambiguous target and exact unsubmitted branch are blocked without submission.

cases.prompt: Sweep exact PR 501. Its first current-head review reports one nit. Address fixes that nit with code, producing a new verified head and resolving the thread. Re-review the new head before declaring the PR clean. Return one JSON object with reviewCalls, heads, ordered events, thread resolution, and status.
cases.expected: The Address-produced head change invalidates the first review even though the finding was a nit, so the new head receives a second review before clean status.

cases.prompt: Sweep exact PR 601 with review_sweep.max_rounds set to 2. Review sha-601-a finds a nit and Address fixes it with code at sha-601-b. Review sha-601-b finds another nit and Address fixes it with code at sha-601-c. Before reviewing sha-601-c, enforce the configured round cap. Return one JSON object with reviewCalls, reviewedHeads, currentHead, events, status, and safeResumeBoundary.
cases.expected: The two configured rounds run, but the second Address-produced head cannot start a third review; the sweep blocks on sha-601-c with an exact resume boundary.

assertions.expected: increase review_sweep.max_rounds above 2, then review PR 601 at sha-601-c

cases.prompt: Classify two sweep configurations without calling GitHub or changing files. Scenario absent has no review_sweep.max_rounds key. Scenario malformed sets review_sweep.max_rounds to zero. In each scenario, a PR keeps producing explained new heads after Address and would otherwise start a fourth Review → Address round. Apply the configured fallback boundary and return exactly one JSON object with absent and malformed objects, each containing cap, warning, reviewCalls, and status.
cases.expected: Both scenarios use the default cap of three and block before a fourth review; only the malformed value emits a warning.
